plain: In ancient Greece, at Eleusis, about 13 miles northwest of Athens, people took part in secret religious rites known as the Eleusinian Mysteries. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says those taking part drank the kykeon, a special drink. He passes on the idea of a writer, Brian Muraresku, that it may have been made with ergot, a grain fungus he says contains LSD. Drawing on Muraresku's book The Immortality Key, Michels says the rites were kept secret on pain of death, and that the little testimony that survives suggests people came away believing they were immortal. Elsewhere he describes the drink as a psychedelic that freed the soul so people could see beings, and he sums up the rites with the saying "if you die before you die, you won't die when you die." A neuroscientist, Andrew Gallimore, also points to Muraresku and says the ritual is where people may have discovered this ergot preparation. So the story comes mostly from the host, again and again, plus one scientist guest, both leaning on Muraresku. If true, it would mean one of the ancient world's great religious rites was built on a mind-altering drug that opened a door to other beings.
